standard_prerequisites.name: Beta distribution density
standard_prerequisites.statement: If Z follows Dir(alpha) then each component Z_i is Beta(alpha_i, 1 - alpha_i) with density proportional to t^{alpha_i - 1}(1-t)^{-alpha_i}.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the display at source lines 1451-1457 that makes the integral of the lemma the quantity to be estimated.

standard_prerequisites.name: Euler reflection formula
standard_prerequisites.use: It is used at source line 1458 and again inside the proof at line 1473 to normalise the total mass to pi.

standard_prerequisites.name: Symmetry of the integrand
standard_prerequisites.statement: The integral and its bound are invariant under (alpha,u) -> (1-alpha, 1-u).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the reduction that opens the proof at source line 1471.

core_obligations: Reduce by the symmetry (alpha,u) -> (1-alpha,1-u) to the case u in [0,1/2] (source line 1471).
Normalise the total mass: sin(pi alpha) times the integral over [0,1] equals pi by the reflection formula, which disposes of the case delta > 1/4 (source lines 1472-1475).

Restrict to alpha in (0,1), u in [0,1/2] and delta in [0,1/4], where 1 - t is bounded below on [0,u+delta], and reduce the claim to the pure power integral displayed as the new goal (source lines 1477-1481).

Treat the case delta <= u/2 by bounding t below by u/2 on the interval of integration, and the case delta >= u/2 by extending the integral to [0,3delta] and evaluating the power integral, which gives the matching order delta^alpha (source lines 1483-1494).

proof_roadmap.step: Symmetry reduction and normalisation, disposing of large delta.
Bound the (1-t)^{-alpha} factor and reduce to a pure power integral.
Case delta <= u/2 by a lower bound on t.
Case delta >= u/2 by extending the range and evaluating the power integral.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `lem:beta estimate` at source lines 1460-1469: a uniform two-sided bound for sin(pi alpha) times the Beta-type integral over [u-delta,u+delta], together with the log-form corollary when delta >= 1/log x. The author's proof (source lines 1471-1496) is a full case analysis rather than an appeal to a standard Beta estimate: it starts with a symmetry reduction (line 1471), normalises the total mass to pi and thereby removes the case delta > 1/4 (lines 1472-1475), reduces the remaining claim to a pure power integral after bounding 1-t below (lines 1477-1481), and then splits into delta <= u/2, where t is bounded below by u/2 (lines 1483-1487), and delta >= u/2, where the integral is extended to [0,3delta] and evaluated to produce delta^alpha (lines 1489-1495). The exponent bookkeeping in the second case, including the comparison delta^alpha ~ delta/(u+delta)^{1-alpha}, is the step that the statement hides.
